title: Skyvar Idle online multiplayer Idler
author: Alltimegamers
selftext:
Hey everyone! I’ve been building Skyvar Idle, an online idle RPG set in the Sundered Isles, a world of floating islands you sail between by airship. It’s now playable in your browser, free for a limited time, and I’d really like feedback from people who play idle games.



Play: [https://play.skyvaridle.com](https://play.skyvaridle.com)

Sign in: Steam, or create an account with a name and password (no email needed).



What’s in it



10 skills: Woodcutting, Mining, Fishing, Farming, Smithing, Cooking, Outfitting, Glyphcraft, Windsailing and Combat. They all train while you’re away.

Your own island: a homestead you build on, with workshops, a farm, a quarry and decorations. Friends can visit and use what you’ve built.

Idle combat with depth: loadouts, talent trees, food, glyphs, and automatic loadout switching.

Multiplayer: dungeons with parties, a world boss everyone fights together, guilds with their own islands, Trade Halls, chat and friends.

Daily tasks, a Renown Store, quests and achievements.

One shared world, with the same server and characters as the Steam version.

How it was built



It’s a small project: me as the designer and director, with an AI (Claude) writing nearly all of the code and doing much of the design work alongside me. The art is AI-generated, with every piece picked and checked by hand. I wanted to be upfront about that, because I know it matters to people here.



The technical side, for the curious:



Engine and code: Godot 4. The same game-rules code runs in the game, on the server and in about 350 automated tests.

The server decides everything, so the browser version is just as fair as the desktop one.

Testing: every change gets automated playtests that click through the real game and take screenshots, plus regular play sessions with friends.

Under the hood: a SQLite database, so trades are saved all at once, never half-done.

Design history: every decision we’ve made is written down in one design document (it’s well past 240 decisions now).

What I’m looking for



Honest feedback: what’s fun, what’s confusing, what feels slow or grindy, and what you’d want next. There’s a Feedback button in the top bar of the game that sends reports straight to me with a screenshot, or just comment here. Phones should work too (you can even add it to your home screen), but that’s the least tested part, so please tell me if something breaks.



It’s coming to Steam in December 2026 if you’d like to wishlist it: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5370390/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5370390/)
